headline: BOTH ROUND-1 BLOCKERS ARE CLOSED AT THE ROOT AND I CONFIRMED EVERY DIGEST THE BUILDER PUBLISHED. THE CONTENT KEY IS RIGHT, AND THE ASSERTION THAT PROVES IT IS THE ONE THING THAT NOW FAILS THE GATE ON VALID INPUT. B1: the amended verdict is recorded with the result its artifact carries (event 246e3bf2c9da, pass_with_notes round 2, verdict_blob 3270b3ae), and the new payload-truth assertion has REAL TEETH, which I measured by mutating the shipped module: a wrong verdict, a wrong round, a wrong reviewed commit and an `at` taken from the wall clock each turn it red, and the read-back genuinely uses `git show HEAD:<path>` through the block's own helper where the module uses `git cat-file blob`, so nothing is self-confirming. B2: six clone shapes of one commit (full, --depth 1, --depth 2, --depth 50, --filter=blob:none, --single-branch) all derive 154 keys at key-set sha256 64a1055dc86dfb0a and `git ls-files -s` is byte-identical at a9430d6ea7d78dab in every one, the three that can append render pending events at 2af38e4b1a0f5b77, --depth 1 and --depth 2 append NOTHING and name the shallow reason with 154 withheld, --depth 50 withholds exactly 135 (the boundary round 1 measured as 135 wrong keys), and a fresh shallow adopter with no earlier events reconciles normally at 3 then 0. THE BLOCKER IS THIS: scripts/selftest.py:21208 asserts the event's `at` EQUALS the artifact's reviewed_at for EVERY artifact in the corpus, and the module's own DECLARED fallback is that an artifact carrying no usable reviewed_at is dated at RECONCILIATION, counted and reported on the stage line. Those two cannot both hold. MEASURED, by committing one artifact: a verdict of exactly the shape of the SHIPPED example `.warp/examples/verdict-example.json`, which declares no reviewed_at and which `validate.py verdict` and `validate.py all` both accept at exit 0, takes the WARP-0722 block to 24 passed / 1 failed while the stage line correctly prints `1 dated at reconciliation (the artifact declares no reviewed_at)`. CHECK_unit is `required:python3 scripts/selftest.py`, so that is a RED gate on a valid artifact, and the one behaviour the manifest names as the sole case where two clones may differ is unreachable without reddening the build. A reviewed_at in any other legal ISO form (`+00:00`) does the same. SECOND, ON THE RECORD ONLY: AC2 as AMENDED THIS ROUND still names `a duplicate key in the log` as its own refutation, and the log it ships with carries exactly one, which the stage reports on every run, while AC2 is dispositioned `passed`. THE TALLY SURPLUS IS STALE RESIDUE AND I PROVED IT BY PROVENANCE, NOT BY ACCEPTING THE EXPLANATION: the log holds 156 verdict events over 155 distinct keys, the duplicated key is (verdict.recorded, WARP-1208, 9e4c38f6) held by TWO OLD-FORM events carrying no verdict_blob, both written by round 1's reconciler, and round 2's code appended exactly two NEW-FORM events and zero on every run since. Six concurrent reconciliations over a 60-verdict fixture produced 60 events, 60 distinct keys and 0 duplicates, against the 180 duplicates round 1 measured from four. A STALE LOCK CANNOT WEDGE THE GATE, and not by luck: the lock is an fcntl.flock on the log file descriptor with no lock FILE to leave behind, so when I SIGKILLed a process holding it the very next run appended the five withheld events. THE CLOSING CLAIM IS TRUE: event 68d1e783901b is `verdict.recorded` for WARP-0722, `fail`, round 1, `at` 2026-07-27T11:05:00Z from the reviewer's own reviewed_at, commit 9b7a58a which is what that review reviewed, and verdict_blob 653f4a312c24 which is `git rev-parse HEAD:proof/WARP-0722/verdict-fail.json`. The projection recorded the review that failed it. GATE GREEN ON MY OWN CLOCK, 3226 / 0, 3:10.92, exit 0, and the floor is clean on every item.
must_fix_before_live: THE PAYLOAD-TRUTH ASSERTION REDDENS THE GATE ON AN ARTIFACT THE CONTRACT ACCEPTS AND THE MODULE DECLARES IT HANDLES. scripts/selftest.py:21202-21209 quantifies `all(...)` over every derived event, and two of its conjuncts are universals the module refutes by design: :21208 `_e.get("at") == head.get("reviewed_at")` is false whenever the artifact declares no reviewed_at, because .warp/events.py:375-378 then dates the event at reconciliation and :436 counts it as `dated_at_reconciliation`; and :21206 `_e.get("reviewed_at") == head.get("reviewed_at")` is false whenever the declared value is a legal ISO timestamp in another form, because :376-377 DELETES the field rather than carrying a format this envelope does not write. CONSTRUCTED AND MEASURED, four planted artifacts committed one at a time into an exact copy of this tree: no reviewed_at gives 24 passed / 1 failed; `2026-07-27T12:00:00+00:00` gives 24 passed / 1 failed; 2099 and a normal date both give 25 passed / 0 failed. `.warp/validate.py` VERDICT_REQ is [schema, spec_id, commit, reviewer, verdict, criteria], reviewed_at is NOT in it, and `validate.py verdict` and `validate.py all` both exit 0 on all four, so the gate is red on an artifact the contract system stamps green. THE TRIGGER IS NOT HYPOTHETICAL: the SHIPPED example a reviewer is told to follow, `.warp/examples/verdict-example.json` and its template copy, declares no reviewed_at (grep count 0 in both), so a verdict written from the example reddens this repository's own build on an assertion about somebody else's data. AND IT MAKES A PUBLISHED BEHAVIOUR UNREACHABLE: checks.the_at_decision declares the fallback as `the ONE case where two clones can differ, in a payload field, never in the key`, and it can never be exercised in this repository without a red gate. RESOLVE IT IN ONE DIRECTION OR THE OTHER, because shipping both is shipping a contradiction. Either narrow the two conjuncts to the artifacts that declare a usable reviewed_at (and assert the fallback's shape on the rest, which is what `dated_at_reconciliation` exists to make checkable), or require reviewed_at in this envelope's format ON THE ARTIFACT in `.warp/validate.py` and delete the fallback and every claim that declares it. The second is where AC2's own evidence 7 says such a rule belongs, since it argues that duplicating the verdict vocabulary inside the projection would be a second vocabulary to drift. The same narrowing is owed to the module's prose, which states the universal and its exception two lines apart: .warp/events.py:348-351 says EVERY substantive field comes from the artifact's bytes `so two clones of one commit render byte-identical events at any depth`, then :355-357 gives the reconciliation-time fallback that makes exactly that false; .warp/events.py:82-85 repeats it in make_event; and the capability note carries it in all EIGHT copies.

AC2 AS AMENDED THIS ROUND NAMES A REFUTATION ITS OWN SHIPPED LOG SATISFIES, AND IS DISPOSITIONED `passed`. The amended text reads `WHAT WOULD REFUTE IT: a duplicate key in the log, ...`, and `.warp/events.jsonl` at HEAD holds 156 verdict events over 155 distinct keys, so the stage prints `1 duplicate key(s) already in the log` on every run and the manifest publishes that fact three times. The duplicate is HONEST RESIDUE and I proved its provenance rather than taking the explanation (see note N2), and AC2's DECLARED paragraph already concedes that a wrong event cannot be withdrawn. That is precisely why the clause has to say what it means: a duplicate key APPENDED BY A RECONCILIATION, or the DECLARED paragraph has to name the pre-existing duplicate the way it names the unresolvable earlier events. This is the same shape round 1 ruled on for AC3, where the answer was to amend the criterion in the spec rather than argue the disposition in a proof, and AC2 is a criterion this build was already rewriting. One clause, in a spec at `status: ready`, in this item's footprint. It is a RECORD defect and not a behaviour defect: no reconciliation of round 2's code appends a duplicate, which I measured directly.

criteria.note: THE SUBSTANCE IS PROVEN AND THE COMPLETENESS MECHANISM OVER-ASSERTS. WHAT I VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY AND FOUND CORRECT: `git ls-files 'proof/*/verdict*.json'` returns 155 at HEAD and tracked_verdicts equals it; the derivation is total, with derivable plus deferred equal to the domain and every deferral carrying its own reason; every derived key is (verdict.recorded, the spec id its own path names, the blob an independent `git ls-files -s` run reports) with 40 hex characters; `--diff-filter` and the corpus size appear ZERO times in all EIGHT copies of .warp/events.py and zero times in the eight gate scripts, where round 1 left `154` in a comment; the type is verdict.recorded, a member of the parsed EVENT_TYPES of both events.py and validate.py; the stage call sits in the always-run built-in section of all eight gate scripts, its block is byte-identical across all eight (sha256 701012b766ee on my own extraction) and mentions FAIL nowhere, guarded with `||`; and the projection's payload equals what the repository committed for all 155 artifacts, which I re-derived myself. THE ROUND-1 DEFECT IS CLOSED ON THE ARTIFACT THAT PRODUCED IT: `git rev-parse HEAD:proof/WARP-1208/verdict.json` is 3270b3ae and the log now carries pass_with_notes round 2 for it (event 246e3bf2c9da, at 2026-07-24T21:20:00Z from the artifact's own reviewed_at, commit 1e81f39b which is the commit that verdict says it reviewed). THE PUBLISHED TALLY IS RIGHT AND I RE-DERIVED IT FROM THE ARTIFACTS, not from the projection: reading every blob `git ls-tree -r 9a5f0b7` names under proof gives 154 artifacts at {pass_with_notes 102, pass 38, fail 14}, exactly what the manifest and the commit message publish, and at HEAD it is 155 at {pass_with_notes 102, pass 38, fail 15}. THE ASSERTION HAS TEETH, WHICH IS THIS ROUND'S CENTRAL NEW TOOTH AND I MUTATION-TESTED IT: forcing the projected verdict to `pass` kills 2 assertions, a round off by one kills 2, an `at` taken from the wall clock kills 1, a wrong reviewed commit kills 1, and the truth side reads through the block's own `_v22_git(ROOT, "show", "HEAD:" + p)` helper at scripts/selftest.py:21199 where the module reads `git cat-file blob` at .warp/events.py:364, two different commands with no shared helper, so agreement cannot come from sharing a mechanism. WHY THIS IS FAILED ANYWAY: the criterion's own HOW COMPLETENESS IS KNOWN clause is that assertion, and as written it is false of the module's declared fallback, so it turns the gate RED on a verdict artifact of exactly the shipped example's shape. See must_fix 1. ONE SMALLER THING IN THE SAME ASSERTION: the wrong-path mutant does not fail, it RAISES a KeyError at scripts/selftest.py:21203, because the comparison indexes `_v22_head_content` by the event's own verdict_path. The gate still goes red (an uncaught exception exits non-zero), but the run reports nothing, and the twenty-four other assertions in the block never execute. A `.get(path, {})` there would make a failure a FAILURE rather than a crash. ON THE TALLY SENTENCE: the manifest says `THE TALLY DERIVED FROM THE EVENTS EQUALS THE TALLY DERIVED FROM THE ARTIFACTS`, and in the assertion (scripts/selftest.py:21210-21219) `the events` means the PROJECTED events and not the log, which cannot equal it while the log holds the pre-existing duplicate. That reading is the only consistent one, since evidence 3 of the same criterion states the log's own count and explains the difference, so I rule it accurate but ambiguous in a sentence that is load-bearing for the number this item publishes.

PASSED ON SUBSTANCE, WITH THE ONE REFUTATION CLAUSE RECORDED AS WRONG (must_fix 2). I REPRODUCED THE WHOLE CLONE MATRIX MYSELF AND EXTENDED IT. Six shapes cloned from one mirror pinned at 9a5f0b7, HEAD verified 9a5f0b7c74f1 in every cell: full, --depth 1, --depth 2, --depth 50, --filter=blob:none, --single-branch. All six derive 154 keys with key-set sha256 64a1055dc86dfb0a, which is the digest the manifest publishes, and `git ls-files -s 'proof/*/verdict*.json' | sha256sum` is a9430d6ea7d78dab in all six, which is the other one. The shallow flag is true in exactly the three shallow cells. The three that can append render pending events at 2af38e4b1a0f5b77, the third published digest. FAIL-CLOSED, DRIVEN END TO END THROUGH THE REAL CLI AND NOT ONLY DRY-RUN: in --depth 1 and --depth 2 the log goes 781 to 781 lines, sha256 unchanged at 73e44d1f6077155b, printing `154 earlier event(s) this repository cannot resolve so 154 append(s) WITHHELD (shallow repository: clone with --depth 0 to reconcile)`; at --depth 50 it withholds exactly 135, the same boundary round 1 measured as 135 WRONG keys, same line and opposite outcome; in the full clone it appends exactly 1 and then 0. THE RULE IS TIED TO THE REAL DEPENDENCY, which I checked rather than assumed: a fixture repository cloned at --depth 1 with NO earlier events appends 3 and then 0, so shallowness alone does not withhold. FOUR SHAPES I ADDED, none of which appends a wrong key or withholds silently: a linked WORKTREE of the full clone derives 64a1055dc86dfb0a with 1 pending, identical to its parent; a repository with a `.git/info/grafts` file grafting the commit that added WARP-1208's verdict derives 64a1055dc86dfb0a with 1 pending, unchanged; a BARE clone reports `0 verdict artifact(s) tracked` and exits 0 without keying anything, since `git ls-files` has no work tree to read; and a `git replace` of that same commit derives the IDENTICAL key set while resolving the legacy event through the replacement, so pending goes 1 to 0 and the correcting event is never appended. That last one is the only asymmetry I found and it is in the safe direction: a rewritten history can SUPPRESS an append, never fabricate a key, and the resolver trusts git at the layer where git is the authority. IDEMPOTENCE AND THE MIGRATION: the log holds 154 old-form events with no verdict_blob and 2 new-form ones; all 154 resolve through `git rev-parse <commit>:<path>`, which is why the fix run appended one line and not 154; five further runs in the real repository appended zero and left the file byte-identical. THE AMEND AND RENAME CLASSES, CONSTRUCTED: a file rename inside a spec directory appends NOTHING; a merge-only add whose verdict is in neither parent is keyed like any other (1 appended); and the byte-identical copy-out appends nothing. THE LOCK IS RIGHT (note N3). THE TWO DECLARED COSTS ARE REAL, I BUILT BOTH AND I ACCEPT BOTH (note N6).

AMENDED IN THE SPEC, NOT REINTERPRETED IN A PROOF, WHICH IS WHAT ROUND 1 ASKED FOR, AND I VERIFIED THE AMENDMENT AGAINST THE DIFF RATHER THAN THE CLAIM. `git diff 9b7a58a 9a5f0b7 -- specs/WARP-0722-...md` shows AC3's letter replaced: it no longer asks for an EMPTY LIST but for the EQUALITY over an enumerated record list, it carries the amendment record and new refutation conditions, and a selftest asserts the amendment on the spec text so it cannot quietly revert. `passed` is now true of the text. The equality itself holds in both directions over every tracked file, and I confirmed the mechanism is a live `git ls-files` read at scripts/selftest.py:21524-21529 rather than a stored list. `Nothing reads these events yet` appears ZERO times in the spec, so round 1's B3 is deleted and not qualified, and the Context sentence that claimed the adding-commit sha is identical everywhere survives only inside the quotation of what it got wrong, followed by the command that refutes it. The record list's WARP-0403 reasons carry both corrections round 1 asked for, one restated as mechanical and one as records policy. ONE RECORD ERROR INSIDE THIS CRITERION'S EVIDENCE: its header says `NOW ELEVEN ENTRIES` and the shipped list at scripts/selftest.py:21493-21524 has TEN, which the same evidence's own body then states correctly. Corrected, not argued.

spec_edit_ruling: THE SPEC WAS EDITED AGAIN THIS ROUND, ALL THREE CRITERIA WERE AMENDED, AND I CHECKED EACH AMENDMENT AGAINST THE DIFF RATHER THAN THE CLAIM. AC1 gained the payload-truth clause and the declaration that two byte-identical artifacts of one spec are ONE review; AC2 replaced the adding-commit key with the content key and recorded the two refutations that forced it, with the fixture run raised from two passes to three; AC3 replaced the unreachable EMPTY LIST with the equality that ships. All three carry an explicit AMENDED IN ROUND 2 record naming what was measured, which is the right form: the criterion changed and says so, rather than a proof arguing that a criterion means something other than what it says. Both spec edits round 1 asked for are done: the Context sentence claiming the adding-commit sha is a property of history identical everywhere is now the refutation, and the AC3 letter is amended. WHAT IS STILL WRONG IN THE SPEC, and it is one clause: AC2's refutation list names `a duplicate key in the log` while the shipped log holds one that the stage reports on every run, so the criterion as amended is contradicted by the state it ships in. That is must_fix 2 and it is the same class round 1 ruled on for AC3. NOT MY EDIT TO MAKE: I changed no file but this verdict, and I ran the gate in an exact copy of the tree so the gated tree carried none of my files.
notes: N1 THE `at` IS NOW AUTHOR-CONTROLLED AND I RULE THE TRADE ACCEPTABLE, DECLARED-COST, NOT A DEFECT, AND UNDER-DECLARED AS SHIPPED. THE FACTS FIRST. `reviewed_at` is validated NOWHERE for a verdict: it is absent from VERDICT_REQ, no format check and no plausibility check exists, and nothing anywhere cross-checks it against the commit that added the artifact, which is not an oversight the module could correct cheaply because it makes NO history call at all (seven git call sites, none of them reads a commit date). MEASURED, by committing planted artifacts: reviewed_at `1970-01-01T00:00:00Z` and `2099-12-31T23:59:59Z` both pass `validate.py verdict` and `validate.py all` at exit 0 and land verbatim in the event's `at` and reviewed_at, in a log that is append-only. THE SURFACE IS ALREADY OCCUPIED IN THE LIVE CORPUS: proof/WARP-1210/verdict-9-fail.json declares reviewed_at 2026-07-28T09:30:00Z, which is a day beyond the wall clock as I write this (2026-07-27T11:43:05Z), so the corpus already carries a review dated in the future and nothing noticed. WHY I STILL RULE IT ACCEPTABLE, on four legs. (1) `at` is a PAYLOAD field and never part of the key, so a forged value cannot cause a duplicate, a missing event, a wrong result or a wrong count; it can only misorder a chronology. I confirmed the blast radius by reading the two consumers: metrics.py sorts by `at` where order matters and its tallies are order-free, and runstatus.py slices by FILE POSITION, so it is already wrong for a pre-existing reason and a forged `at` does not make it worse. (2) The builder's reasoning against both alternatives holds and I checked it: the adding-commit date is exactly the history-dependent lookup B2 blocked and becomes the grafted tip's date in a shallow clone, and reconciliation time would have stamped 154 reviews with one minute. Of the three candidates only reviewed_at is both content-derived and the right fact. (3) Author control of `at` is not new information in this design. The verdict, the round, the reviewer and the reviewed commit are ALL author-chosen and all projected verbatim, and the item's premise is that the artifact is the durable truth. A reviewer who would forge a timestamp would forge a pass, and the vocabulary check that stops the second (verified: a planted TOTALLY-BOGUS-VALUE is refused by `validate.py verdict` and by `validate.py all` at exit 1) is on the ARTIFACT, which is where the analogous guard for reviewed_at belongs. (4) The chronology it buys is real and prospective. WHAT IS OWED, AND IT IS THE PART THAT IS MISSING: nowhere in the spec, the manifest or the capability note is the field named as author-controlled and unvalidated. checks.the_at_decision argues chronology, reproducibility and the fallback, and never says that the chronology this log now publishes is exactly as honest as its reviewers. Declare it, and record the artifact-side item (require reviewed_at in this envelope's format in `.warp/validate.py`), which is the same one line that resolves must_fix 1 in its second direction.

N2 THE TALLY SURPLUS IS STALE RESIDUE FROM ROUND 1'S SUPERSEDED KEY SCHEME, NOT A LIVE DEFECT, AND I ESTABLISHED IT BY PROVENANCE RATHER THAN BY ACCEPTING THE EXPLANATION. `.warp/events.jsonl` at HEAD holds 786 events of which 156 are verdict.recorded. Resolving every one of the 156 to its content key gives 155 DISTINCT keys and exactly one duplicated pair: (verdict.recorded, WARP-1208, 9e4c38f64987e9fb7386ff80299fc2736a0d3d9b), held by the event for proof/WARP-1208/verdict.json at commit 03de88f and the event for proof/WARP-1208/verdict-1-fail.json at commit 17ca8dd. BOTH ARE OLD-FORM: neither carries a verdict_blob, so both were written by round 1's reconciler under (path, adding commit), where they were two distinct keys. Under the content key they collapse to one, because verdict-1-fail.json is a byte-identical copy of what verdict.json held before it was amended. Round 2's code appended exactly TWO events, both NEW-FORM (246e3bf2c9da and 68d1e783901b), and every run since appends zero. So the surplus `fail` is honest historical residue that no append-only log can remove. IS `1 duplicate key(s) already in the log` ON EVERY RUN AN ACCEPTABLE STEADY STATE? YES, WITH ONE ITEM RECORDED, and the reason is that the wart lands on a LIVE READER, not only on a stage line. `python3 .warp/metrics.py` publishes `verdicts: {'pass_with_notes': 102, 'pass': 38, 'fail': 16}` over the log at HEAD, against the 155 artifacts' {pass_with_notes 102, pass 38, fail 15}, so the surface a human reads through /warp:status over-reports fails by one, permanently, and nothing dedupes it. The item does the right thing by deriving its published number from the artifacts and naming the log's own count beside it. The remaining fix is reader-side dedup by event key in metrics.py, which is out of this footprint and is a recorded item, not a reason to hold this round. ONE SIGNAL THAT IS NOT PUBLISHED AND IS IN THE SAME FAMILY: the stage reports duplicate keys IN THE LOG but not duplicate keys IN THE CORPUS. In the collapse fixture (N6) two artifacts sharing a blob report `2 verdict artifact(s) tracked, 1 already recorded, 0 derivable but not appended` and nothing says one artifact was absorbed. It is one count (derivable keys against derivable paths) and this item's own principle is to publish every non-zero integrity signal.

N3 THE LOCK IS RIGHT AND A STALE LOCK CANNOT WEDGE THE GATE, NOT BY LUCK BUT BY CONSTRUCTION. It is `fcntl.flock(fh.fileno(), LOCK_EX | LOCK_NB)` taken on the LOG FILE ITSELF at .warp/events.py:396-407, so there is no lock file, no pid file and nothing to go stale: the kernel drops the lock when the holding descriptor closes, including on process death. MEASURED, three ways. A live holder: the CLI prints `5 derivable but not appended, NOT appended (held by another reconciliation)`, exits 0, and the log goes 1 to 1 line; a second attempt while still held does the same. The holder SIGKILLed: the very next run appends all five withheld events, so the withheld work is not lost and nothing waits. And no artefact is left in `.warp/` afterwards. SIX GENUINELY CONCURRENT reconciliations over a 60-verdict fixture: exactly ONE reported `60 appended` and the other five reported NOT appended, the log ended with 60 verdict events over 60 distinct keys and 0 duplicates, and the settling run reported `60 already recorded, 0 appended`. Round 1 measured 180 duplicates from four concurrent runs, so that class is closed. Non-blocking was the right call and the failure mode it trades into (an append deferred to the next run) is the cheapest one available.

N4 THE PAYLOAD-TRUTH ASSERTION HAS REAL TEETH AND IS NOT SELF-CONFIRMING, WHICH I MEASURED BY MUTATION RATHER THAN BY READING IT. Against an exact copy of the tree, with the WARP-0722 block extracted and run standalone (25 passed / 0 failed in 1.2s on the pristine copy, matching the manifest's 25 in 1.17s): forcing the projected `verdict` to `pass` kills the payload assertion AND the amend-in-place assertion (23 passed / 2 failed); adding one to the projected `round` kills the same two; taking `at` from the wall clock instead of reviewed_at kills the payload assertion (24 / 1); a fabricated reviewed commit kills it (24 / 1); and a wrong verdict_path raises rather than fails, which is the smaller finding recorded under AC1. THE MECHANISMS ARE GENUINELY DIFFERENT AND SHARE NOTHING: the truth side is `_v22_git(ROOT, "show", "HEAD:" + p)` at scripts/selftest.py:21199, a helper defined in the block at :21087, while the module reads `_git(["cat-file", "blob", blob])` at .warp/events.py:364. One reads HEAD's tree by path and the other reads a blob by sha, and the two can only agree if the index blob and the HEAD blob are the same object, which is exactly what excluding staged paths at .warp/events.py:228-240 guarantees.

N5 THE init_scaffold REGRESSION: I RULE THE DEFERRAL LEGITIMATE, AND NARROWLY, BECAUSE THE SCAFFOLD PATH IS NOT WORSE THAN IT WAS. I reproduced it: `python3 .warp/init_scaffold.py <fresh repo>` creates 40 files, reports `substrate complete`, lays no `.warp/events.py`, and its gate then prints `python3: can't open file ... .warp/events.py: [Errno 2] No such file or directory` above `review events: reconciliation unavailable (python3 or .warp/events.py) - by design not a gate failure`, on every run, forever, with GATE: GREEN. The re-classification is correct and it IS a regression this item introduced, since before it verify.sh appended its gate event with a bare printf and never invoked the module. WHY IT DOES NOT BLOCK, on three legs I checked rather than accepted. FIRST, THE SCAFFOLD NEVER CARRIED THE EVENTS SUBSYSTEM AT ALL: `_FILES` at .warp/init_scaffold.py:39-64 omits events.py, metrics.py, runstatus.py and incident.py alike, so a scaffolded repository had no verdict events before this item and has none after. It gains a console line and loses nothing, where a pack adopter gains the projection (all 6 packs plus plugin/templates carry the module byte-identical at 9fc4c5afb96fd55d, and check_pack_drift.py holds it). SECOND, the false-capability worry does not land on this item: `.warp/capabilities.yaml` IS scaffolded and has declared `event_envelope_v1` with home `.warp/events.py` since before this item, and nothing validates that a capability's home exists, so that mismatch is pre-existing. THIRD, it fails SAFE: no wrong key, no wrong count, no green stamp on a false statement, and the line says `unavailable` in plain words. IT IS ALSO TWO LINES (one in `_FILES`, one in `REQUIRED_SUBSTRATE`) in a file outside this footprint, and the shape gate refuses a diff outside the footprint, so fixing it here means widening the footprint of a spec whose push is already gated on a protected-path approval. Recording it as a regression this item introduced, with its own item, is the honest disposition. WHAT I WOULD NOT ACCEPT and do not have to: if the scaffold path had LOST a working capability, or if the fallback were silent, this would block.

N6 THE TWO DECLARED COSTS OF BLOB KEYING, BOTH CONSTRUCTED, BOTH ACCEPTED. (a) TWO BYTE-IDENTICAL VERDICTS OF ONE SPEC COLLAPSE TO ONE EVENT. Built it in the only shape that makes it reachable: two reviews of one spec written to the SHIPPED example's shape, with no round and no reviewed_at, agreeing on spec, commit, reviewer and verdict. Two artifacts, ONE event, and the second run reports `2 verdict artifact(s) tracked, 1 already recorded`. I ACCEPT IT. Two artifacts that agree in every recorded field are indistinguishable to every consumer of the log, so what is lost is a row no reader could have told apart, and the alternative is a discriminator that is either the path (which is the defect round 1 shipped) or a counter (which is not content-addressed and would break the clone identity that closes B2). ONE COUPLING WORTH RECORDING: the collapse is unreachable while every verdict carries a reviewed_at to the second, which is today's convention, and it becomes reachable the moment must_fix 1 is resolved in the direction of keeping the fallback. I confirmed the boundary: the same two reviews with reviewed_at differing by ONE SECOND get two events. (b) RENAMING A SPEC DIRECTORY RE-KEYS EVERY EVENT. Built it: three rounds under proof/SP-1, then `git mv proof/SP-1 proof/SP-9`, and the next run appends 3 more events, 6 over 3 artifacts. `HONEST RATHER THAN HARMLESS` UNDERSTATES WHAT SHIPS, IN THE ITEM'S FAVOUR: the run also prints `3 superseded review(s) on record`, so the doubling is PUBLISHED on the stage line rather than silent, and a file rename inside the same spec directory appends nothing. disposition: DO NOT LAND IT YET, AND THE GAP IS ONE ASSERTION WIDE. THIS ROUND FIXED WHAT IT SET OUT TO FIX AND I COULD NOT BREAK IT. The key identifies a REVIEW, and the property was attacked before it was adopted: the (spec id, path, blob) candidate was rejected for the right reason, because the path moves under a rename this repository has already performed. I reproduced all three published digests byte for byte across six clone shapes and added four more shapes that did not move them; the amended verdict now records the result its artifact carries; the fail-closed rule is tied to the real dependency rather than to shallowness as a proxy, in both directions; the lock is correct and cannot wedge; the tally is re-derived from the artifacts and is right; the two criteria were amended IN THE SPEC; and the closing claim is true, so the projection recorded the review that failed its first round. WHAT BLOCKS IS THE TOOTH ITSELF, AIMED ONE NOTCH TOO WIDE. scripts/selftest.py:21208 asserts the event's `at` equals the artifact's reviewed_at for EVERY artifact in the corpus, while the module deliberately dates an artifact with no usable reviewed_at at reconciliation, counts it, and reports it. Those cannot both be true, and the artifact that breaks the tie is not exotic: it is the shape of the SHIPPED verdict example, which declares no reviewed_at and which every validator accepts. Committing one takes the block to 24 passed / 1 failed, and CHECK_unit is required, so that is a RED GATE ON A VALID ARTIFACT and the one behaviour the manifest names as the sole case where two clones may differ can never be exercised here without reddening the build. Narrow the two conjuncts to the artifacts that declare a usable reviewed_at and assert the fallback's shape on the rest, or require reviewed_at on the ARTIFACT in validate.py and delete the fallback with every claim that declares it. Either is small; shipping both is shipping a contradiction. The same narrowing is owed to the module's own prose, which states the byte-identical-at-any-depth universal and its exception two lines apart, in all eight copies. THE SECOND ITEM IS A RECORD FIX OF THE SHAPE ROUND 1 RULED ON: AC2 as amended this round still names `a duplicate key in the log` as its own refutation, and the log it ships with holds one, reported on every run. Say `appended by a reconciliation`, or name the pre-existing duplicate in the DECLARED paragraph the way the unresolvable earlier events are named. ON THE `at` TRADE, WHICH I WAS ASKED TO RULE AND DO: the tamper surface is real, it is wider than the record admits (no format check, no plausibility check, no cross-check against the adding commit, and a future-dated review already sitting in the corpus), and it is still ACCEPTABLE, because `at` is payload and never key, because both alternatives are worse for reasons this item measured, and because every other substantive field is equally author-chosen. What is owed is the declaration, plus the recorded artifact-side item that would close it and must_fix 1 in one line.
